text:
anita.support: FYI customer acme-inc opened a support ticket: intermittent 401s on our API (/v1/generate). Started ~09:12 UTC after they reported an IdP key rotation. Logs show: "sig verify failed: no matching key for kid 'abc123'". Can we triage?

mira.sre: Thanks — can you paste a sample Authorization header (redact token body)? Also did they say this affects all tokens or just some users?

anita.support: Pasted sample (redacted): `Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6ImFiYzEyMyJ9.<payload>.<sig>` They say ~30% of calls fail, mostly from EU region. Others succeed.

jamal.eng: Repro steps from their side? curl command?

anita.support: They ran: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` and saw 401 with body: `{"error":"invalid_signature","reason":"no_matching_key_for_kid"}`

deploy-bot: idp-ops-bot rotated JWKS for issuer https://idp.acme.example/.well-known/jwks.json at 2026-03-03T09:06:12Z (rotation-id=rot-20260303-01). Cache-control: max-age=300

dan.sec: Two likely suspects: 1) JWKS cache still contains old entries and our verifier doesn't fetch on kid-miss, 2) IdP rotated keys and new tokens use new kid while some downstream caches still present old kid. Also check clock skew + alg mismatch.

mira.sre: Looked at our verification path: by default we cache JWKS per issuer for 10m and only refresh on TTL expiry, but we should also attempt a refetch if kid not found (we currently do NOT for safety reasons). That explains intermittent.

jamal.eng: Logs from the verifier show: `jwks_cache.get(issuer) -> cache_hit, keys=[...old-key-list...]` then `verify(token) -> lookup_kid('abc123') -> not found -> reject`. No network fetch.

dan.sec: Can we push a safe emergency patch to attempt a single JWKS refetch on kid-miss (with rate limit), plus a quick config to lower cache ttl for 1 hour? That will address recent rotations without huge risk. Also add leeway for iat/exp? any clock skew reports?

anita.support: Customer says their token issued_at ~09:05 UTC, so within seconds of rotation. They didn't mention device clock issues.

mira.sre: I'm +1 for the single-refetch on kid-miss with exponential backoff and local rate-limit per issuer (e.g., 1 fetch per 5s). Quick patch: in verifier, on kid not found -> call fetch_jwks(issuer, force=true) -> update cache -> retry lookup once. If still missing, return original error. I'll prepare rollout to staging.

jamal.eng: Also add better logging: when kid-miss triggers fetch, log old cache age and response headers (cache-control, age) so we can see if CDN cached stale JWKS.

dan.sec: We should also inspect response headers from idp-ops-bot rotation: if their JWKS endpoint returns stale Cache-Control or missing ETag, CDNs could serve older payloads. Ping idp-ops to validate.

idp-ops-bot: Confirmed rotation completed. Their CDN (fastedge) had a short propagation lag — purged at 09:07:50Z. JWKS first published at 09:06:12Z. Some clients may have seen old cache until 09:08.

mira.sre: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) deploy single-refetch-on-kid-miss hotfix (rollout canary 10%, 1h), 2) temporarily reduce jwks_cache_ttl to 60s for all issuers for next 30 minutes, 3) add 120s leeway on token verification for this issuer only (config flag).

dan.sec: Also add incident note for compliance: record why we did forced refetch and leeway. We'll revert leeway after confirmation.

anita.support: I'll inform customer: we're rolling a hotfix to try a refetch on kid-miss and may ask them to retry failing requests; ask them to provide a failing token sample (we can redact) if this persists.

jamal.eng: I have a draft PR for single-refetch behavior and the rate-limit guard. Will push tests covering: missing kid with fresh JWKS containing new kid, and case where kid truly absent -> ensure no DNS/SSRF vector.

mira.sre: Good. After canary looks good I'll increase rollout. Keep me posted on metrics (401 spike, fetch rates).

anita.support: Customer says retrying helped for some calls. We'll keep ticket open until fully resolved. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy request created: PR #4532 -> canary 10% -> started 2845567925

jamal.eng: Updated PR with extra log lines and a safe fetch timeout (2s).

dan.sec: Postmortem actions: (A) enable kid-miss refetch with rate limits, (B) add monitoring for sudden jwks cache misses per issuer, (C) document incident runbook for 3rd-party key rotation.

mira.sre: I'll draft the postmortem after we confirm fixes. Closing note: this class of failure is predictable — verifier design should favor a single on-demand refresh path for kid-miss to handle coordinated rotations.
